study_badge: POPULATION SURVEILLANCE COHORT · 1.84M PERSON-YEARS · STROBE · SYNTHETIC DATA
title: Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure, Urban Heat Islands, and Incident Adult-Onset Asthma Across 14 Metropolitan Cohorts (2016–2025)
authors_line: Mateo Alvarez, ScD¹; Amina Darwish, PhD²; Kenji Takahashi, MD, MPH¹
affiliations_line: ¹Global Environmental Epidemiology Consortium; ²Center for Satellite Climate Exposure Modeling (Synthetic Demonstration Study)

stages.title: 1-km Satellite Exposure
stages.detail: Rolling 36-month aerosol optical depth PM2.5 & nocturnal UHI anomalies

stages.title: Clinical Ascertainment
stages.detail: Validated spirometry + ≥2 controller fills + ED/hospital records

stages.title: Synergy Modeling
stages.detail: Time-varying Poisson regression + additive RERI interaction

items.title: 01  Public Health Context & Aim
paragraphs: Fine particulate pollution (PM2.5) and urban heat island (UHI) warming co-concentrate in dense metropolitan neighborhoods, amplifying airway oxidative stress [1].
bullets: Objective: Quantify independent and joint associations of chronic PM2.5 and nocturnal UHI intensity with adult-onset asthma across 1.84 million person-years.

items.title: 02  Exposure & Statistical Methods
bullets: Exposures: Ensemble satellite-monitor PM2.5 (μg/m³) and warm-season nocturnal surface temperature anomaly (°C vs. rural buffer).
Models: Multivariable quasi-Poisson survival models adjusted for age, sex, smoking pack-years, BMI, greenness (NDVI), and neighborhood deprivation index.
Effect Modification: Relative Excess Risk due to Interaction (RERI) quantified departure from additivity [2].

items.title: Synergistic Air-Heat Respiratory Risk
paragraphs: Overall incidence was 4.84 per 1,000 person-years (8,912 cases). Each +10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increased asthma risk by 24% overall (IRR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18–1.31), rising to 38% in high-UHI neighborhoods.

items.title: 04  Stratified Multivariable Models
items.footnote: Adjusted for age, sex, smoking, BMI, NDVI greenness, and area deprivation.

items.title: 05  Limitations & Policy Implications
bullets: Limitation: Residential geocoding omits workplace indoor air filtration and transit exposure.
Policy Action: Co-targeting PM2.5 emissions and urban heat mitigation in high-UHI districts could avert an estimated 19.4% of attributable adult-onset cases.
